newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB says could set Sfr limit if EMU turmoil.
newsitem.headline: SNB says could set Sfr limit if EMU turmoil.

text.p: The Swiss National Bank (SNB) reiterated it could set a temporary upper limit for the Swiss franc if speculative flows boosted the currency's value sharply around the introduction of Europe's single currency in 1999.

Markets are the most efficient way to adjust exchange rates, SNB director Bruno Gehrig said in a text prepared for delivery to a symposium, adding it was "deeply unrealistic" to expect the SNB to safeguard the franc "like a mother hen".
"But an exceptional situation can arise under some circumstances, where a wave of increased demand leads to overvaluing the Swiss franc, which threatens to damage our economy," Gehrig said.

"In such a situation we would have to loosen our policy with the aim of lowering interest rates and correcting the franc's rise. If need be, we could back up such intervention by stating a temporary upper limit and making the required franc sales."

SNB officials made clear at their news conference in December that they were prepared to take action if the franc soared as a perceived safe-haven currency for investors afraid the single currency would be weak.

Gehrig acknowledged daily Swiss franc turnover on markets, at more than 80 billion francs, was nearly three times larger than Switzerland's entire central bank money supply, but said this should not spawn "false scepticism" of the SNB's power.

"There is no doubt: a central bank can always weaken its currency because it can create and put into cirulation its own money to a theoretically unlimited extent by buying foreign currencies," he said.
